utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Brdjanin. Are you hearing me in a language that you can understand? THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you. The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, General Talic's microphone is on. General Talic, good morning to you can you hear me in a thank that you can understand? THE ACCUSED TALIC: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We may have the case called now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm tempted to say the usual, Your Honour, but it's Joanna Korner and Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, John Ackerman with Tania Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Ackerman. And appearances for General Talic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PITRON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, this is Maitre Michel Pitron and Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic and Fabien Masson for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. Are there any preliminaries you would like to thrash before we bring the witness in? Okay. So let's get it over and done with hoping you will finish your cross-examination today, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Usher? And we go into closed session first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have a couple of minutes to organise ourselves for tomorrow. We having been taken by surprise as much as you have, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first thing I'm going to do is call Mr. Inayat to deal with the search of the railway station -- the radio station, so that Mr. Ackerman can put such questions as he wants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, as for the rest of the day, Your Honour, outstanding matters are the question of Variant A/B, but I tend to agree with Mr. Ackerman we may as well wait to see what happens in the Samac case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To be frank, I haven't discussed it as yet with my two colleagues but my feeling at the time when you were discussing this yesterday was that it would be wiser to wait until we see how it develops Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the other trial, and then we take it up from there if needs be, or else wait until it goes -- covers the whole journey.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, outstanding is still the matter of the -- but it's really only a question of a date to try and organise the hearing of the application to set aside the witness summons for the journalist. I think that's just a question of organising a date. We are going to reply to the -- both Rule 92 submissions, Mr. Ackerman on effectively the principles, and Madam Fauveau applying the principles we suggest to her objections. That will go in today. And really, that's it, other than the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the documents, we will come to that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the ways of doing it, if I've got Mr. Inayat here, is really to just look at the ones that haven't been dealt with. The fourth volume effectively all relates to matters of the military, they are military documents, and they will be dealt with, we hope, to a large extent by Colonel Selak when he testifies so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is he a protected witness or isn't he?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, he's not. The other matter that remains is the testimony of -- I'm sorry, the application to read the dead Colonel Klenc [phoen], but I think logically that will have to follow after Colonel Selak's evidence. So what I'm going to suggest and perhaps Your Honours may like to consider it overnight - obviously, I'm in Your Honours' hands - is that when Mr. Inayat is finished testifying over the search of the radio station, and being cross-examined on it, he should then remain in the witness box effectively as just a conduit so we can look at some of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it -- my recommendation would be that we deal with Mr. Inayat and adjourn. There is a great deal of work that I have to do with regard to documents the Prosecutor has given me that I haven't had a chance to process yet, the response to their motion regarding the depositions. There are just a number of things I would like to try to get finished before I leave here. It might be helpful, Your Honours, if you would assure Ms. Korner that you will read the exhibits, because she's quite nervous apparently that you won't read them, in spite of what you tell her, and is insisting on reading them to you. And I just think that's an incredible waste of our time and I trust Your Honours to read the exhibits. I don't insist on reading all of mine to you, and I just think that it wastes the time in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will take that up. Maybe we will agree with you tomorrow. It depends. Basically, I still want to hear what Ms. Korner has to say and then we will take it up from there. Why should I decide here and now that that's going -- that that's how it's going to be?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Leaving aside the fact that Mr. Ackerman appears to think that by making it sound that I personally am insulting Your Honour's word on this, it is my view as someone who has dealt with document cases, that however much, even as counsel, one reads documents, it's not always that easy, in reading them in bulk, to take them in. There are certain strands that appear, and the documents, particularly in Banja Luka, are exceedingly important, and that's the only reason, but as I say, I am entirely content to abide by Your Honours' decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will probably reach some sort of a compromise tomorrow. My attention -- Madam Registrar is really looking anxiously.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't think there is anything else in this Chamber today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in any case, we have the interpreters, they have been here for a long time and their task is as difficult, if not more difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I say just very quickly, because you're going to be thinking about this overnight, if what Ms. Korner said is rather than reading documents to you, she wants to point out the various strands --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- that's argument and she should not be making argument at this point in the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying we will visit it tomorrow. Adjourned to tomorrow morning. I thank you. I'm sorry once more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.49 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of March, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
